-s8QUpx_Zo4.name: Fly Brain Imaged at Nanoscale Resolution
-s8QUpx_Zo4.description: Scientists at HHMI’s Janelia Research Campus have taken detailed pictures of the entire brain of an adult female fruit fly using transmission electron microscopy. Read more: https://www.janelia.org/news/complete-fly-brain-imaged-at-nanoscale-resolution

-x0WAkQgOJk.name: Inside the fruit fly brain and what it might mean for human health, with Greg Jefferis | Wellcome
-x0WAkQgOJk.description: The inner workings of the human brain are still a mystery to us. For example, we don’t know exactly how individual neurons work together to solve complex problems.

2uMQG5LHWwc.name: The History of Fruit Fly Connectomics at Janelia
2uMQG5LHWwc.description: In 2008, scientists at Janelia Research Campus set out to construct a complete wiring diagram of the brain, otherwise known as a “connectome,” for the fruit fly, Drosophila. With more than 100,000 neurons, the fruit fly brain was hundreds of times larger than that of the previous organism for which a connectome had been constructed.

8nZTq0fJUFc.name: Dazzling Fruit Fly Neurons
8nZTq0fJUFc.description: These dazzling neurons belong to a fruit fly. Confocal microscopy images of them were taken & combined by researchers at our Janelia Research Campus like pieces of a puzzle to build a rough map of the ventral nerve cord (VNC) — the insect equivalent of a spinal cord that coordinates walking, flying, & reflex. _____

9xHZkMxfB0o.name: High-speed, 3D SCAPE Microscope Captures Stunning, Live Videos of Fruit Fly Nerve Cells in Action
9xHZkMxfB0o.description: Columbia engineers and neuroscientists have joined forces to create 3D videos of individual nerve cells moving, stretching and switching on inside free-roaming fruit fly larvae as they move. Data gleaned from these videos reveals how nerve cells called proprioceptive neurons work together to help the body sense where it is in space. To accomplish this feat, the researchers harnessed SCAPE, a cutting-edge microscope developed at Columbia that images neurons at lightning-fast speeds.

CZpaTCuSQao.name: BigData IV: Visualizing, Sharing and Annotating Large Image Data in the Cloud -NEUBIAS Academy @Home
CZpaTCuSQao.description: BIG DATA IV: Visualizing, Sharing and Annotating Large Image Data in the Cloud 3 February, 2021 Catmaid and MoBIE Presenters: Tom Kazimiers, Open Source Research Software Engineer at kazmos GmbH (DE); Chris Barnes, MRC LMB, Cambridge (UK); Albert Cardona, Programme Leader at MRC LMB, Cambridge (UK); Christian Tischer, Bioimage Analyst at EMBL, Heidelberg (DE); Kimberly Meechan, PhD candidate at EMBL (DE); Constantin Pape, PhD candidate at EMBL (DE).

F4lc9cY4fMM.name: Building a fly brain (HD)
F4lc9cY4fMM.description: What is a fruit fly brain made of? In this video we build a fly brain by putting ~18,000 neurons one by one into their places. These 18,000 neurons account for ~20% of the estimated total neurons in a fly brain.

FfhAgQLxx0Q.name: Virtual Fly Brain: Hacking the Fly Connectome Workshop 2021
FfhAgQLxx0Q.description: Interested to learn how to query and analyse fly connectomics data across different data sources? Virtual Fly Brain (https://virtualflybrain.org) ran a free online workshop, 'Hacking the Connectome'

J2xTkMsZchs.name: The FlyWire Connectome
J2xTkMsZchs.description: Neuronal wiring diagram of a whole brain, Nature 2024: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07558-y

OmwXCGPBhNo.name: MetaCell Showcase
OmwXCGPBhNo.description: Some extracts from different tools we developed.

TBCcwWMRcww.name: Explore The BANC (Brain and Nerve Cord) Dataset, part 2
TBCcwWMRcww.description: A tour through the brain and nerve cord connectome (BANC), revealing what it has taught scientists about the organization of sensory-motor circuits, across a whole central nervous system. The most extensive connectome to date!

XJGzoSSihaI.name: Virtual Fly Brain: every fly connectome, image and gene in one place
XJGzoSSihaI.description: Virtual Fly Brain (VFB) is the hub for Drosophila neuroanatomy, imaging data and connectomics: one anatomy ontology behind every dataset, every life stage, the whole nervous system. This tour shows what is in it and the four ways in — browser, Python/R, your own AI assistant over MCP, and VFB Chat. Everything on screen is drawn from live VFB records.

XqrmATUvHac.name: Male Fly Brain Connectome
XqrmATUvHac.description: The male CNS connectome will allow researchers to compare male and female brains and understand complex social behaviors — like mating and aggression — that can vary by sex.

cyWdrbK3di4.name: Fruit Fly Optic Neurons
cyWdrbK3di4.description: Like pinpointing a needle in a haystack, this video shows the connections in a simple neural circuit among the sea of neurons surrounding it. The neurons are part of the fruit fly eye and optic lobe – the part of the brain that processes visual information. The neurons form a basic neural circuit involved in motion detection and hazard evasion. _____

jeh9czULwH0.name: Completing the CNS Connectome
jeh9czULwH0.description: The newly completed connectome is the first map of an entire male fruit fly central nervous system, comprising all the neurons in the brain, both optic lobes, and ventral nerve cord.

k-HQA3eoEgQ.name: Explore the fly BANC (Brain and Nerve Cord) Connectome
k-HQA3eoEgQ.description: A tour through the brain and nerve cord connectome (BANC), revealing what it has taught scientists about the organization of sensory-motor circuits, across a whole central nervous system. The most extensive connectome to date!

m8cmKREXpcw.name: Fruit fly brain simulation
m8cmKREXpcw.description: Fruit fly brain simulation. The simulation is performed by the Flysim simulator developed in Chung-Chuan Lo lab at National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan. The model circuits and parameters were derived from the data available in the FlyCircuit database (http://www.flycircuit.tw/).

mcZwH5MYkFU.name: The Brain: What For? - Albert Cardona - Seminar for Non-Scientists
mcZwH5MYkFU.description: The brain: What for? By Albert Cardona LMB Seminar for Non-Scientists Cambridge Biomedical Campus on Virtual Tour

p4MH4-I-P5I.name: eFIB-SEM volume of a fruit fly larval brain
p4MH4-I-P5I.description: Enhanced FIB-SEM volume acquired at the MRC LMB in the lab of Albert Cardona, showing a brief fly-through of the fruit fly larval brain (Drosophila melanogaster) imaged at 8x8x8 nanometre resolution.

ucF3ofIBj-I.name: Feature Detection in Drosophila Neuron
ucF3ofIBj-I.description: The brain of the fly Drosophila melanogaster processes sensory features in parallel. New research from the Card lab at Janelia uncovers how select visual features are integrated by a downstream descending neuron to bias which escape maneuver a fly executes when a predator approaches.

z2Cre6avnpk.name: VFB2.1 demonstration
z2Cre6avnpk.description: A quick demonstration of how the Virtual Fly Brain V2.1 site can help you find what you're looking for.
